SUTS-001 — SuperUnicode Collation Algorithm

The first SuperUnicode Technical Specification: UCA (UTS #10) equivalence over 64-bit SUCS.

SUTS-001 (SUCA) is the first SuperUnicode Technical Specification. It defines a full UTS #10 (UCA)-equivalent multilevel collation algorithm for the entire 64-bit SuperUnicode character space (sucs_ex_char_t), including the extSUCS plugin ranges above 0x7FFFFFFF.

Algorithm

  1. Normalize (S1) — decompose input to NFD; algorithmic Hangul; canonical ordering.
  2. Map (S2) — walk the string, longest-match contractions and expansions, then simple/implicit CEs; apply variable weighting.
  3. Form sort key (S3) — L1–L4 with level separators, backward secondary support, optional identical level.
  4. Compare (S4) — binary compare of sort keys; identical level resolves by native codepoint order.
Feature Status
At least 3 collation levels + identical Yes — L1–L4 + identical
Canonical equivalence (NFD) Yes
Contractions & expansions Yes
Variable weighting (shifted/blanked/non-ignorable/shift-trimmed) Yes
Backward secondary (French) Yes
Implicit weights for unassigned/Han/native/plugin Yes (algorithmic, 64-bit codepoint)
Tailoring rules (& base < x, <<, <<<, =) Yes (programmatic)
extSUCS 64-bit compatibility Yes

Reference implementation: include/suts/suts_suca.h + src/suts/suts_suca.c (freestanding C99, no heap), registered as suts_static. Data: collation/SUCA.txt, collation/ExtUCA.txt.

Source of truth: docs/suts/SUTS-001-suca.md in the repository. This Technical Report introduces SUCA; SUTR-2 covers the same ground as the original report.
